- ✅ 2026-07-01 M11 input scale source-to-screen boundary gate: added the inverse helper `M11_MapSourcePointToPresentedForPresentation()` (declared in `include/main_loop_m11.h` next to its existing sibling, defined in `src/engine/m11_game_input_mapping.c`) used by touch overlay hit-tests, HUD button bounds, and mouse cursor positions on the presented surface. The new helper clamps the source coordinate to `[0..319] x [0..199]` **before** the `src * targetW` multiply so a caller-supplied out-of-range value (e.g. `1000000 * 3840 = 3.84e9`, beyond `INT_MAX`) cannot overflow on 4K V2.2 presentations; the post-multiply clamp then keeps the result inside `[0..targetW-1] x [0..targetH-1]`. Same target-extent resolution rules as the existing inverse: V1_ORIGINAL = passthrough / return 0, V20_FILTERED = always 640x400, V21_UPSCALED / V22_MODERN = user-selected with positive-extent requirement. - ✅ 2026-06-29 DM1 V1 PC 3.4 native save LSV-02 per-game versioned manifest gate (gapbug_20260629_dm1_save_export_import_manifest_gate): extended `memory_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` (LSV-01) with a 16-byte versioned manifest slot in `AdditionalData[0..15]` of the PC 3.4 `DM_SAVE_HEADER` — a region the original ReDMCSB engine never inspects, so vanilla DM 3.4 PC interop stays intact while Firestaff's importer gains a per-game compatibility gate. Manifest layout (LE, written into meta[41..48] in the obfuscated header half): `LSV01RDM` magic (8 bytes ASCII) + `formatVersion` (uint16, currently 1) + `gameCode` (uint16: 0x00D1=DM1, 0x00C5=CSB, 0x00D2=DM2, 0x00D9=NEXUS, 0x00D4=THERON) + `dungeonCode` (echoes `C10_DUNGEON_DM`) + reserved flags. The exporter (`F0795_SAVEGAME_ExportPC34_Compat`) now stamps the manifest with `gameCode=DM1` by default, the importer (`F0796_SAVEGAME_ImportPC34_Compat`) refuses any manifest with a non-DM1 gameCode (returns `SAVEGAME_PC34_ERROR_BAD_MAGIC`), and three new public helpers wire the per-game gate: `F0799_SAVEGAME_PC34PeekManifest_Compat` (manifest presence + version + gameCode + body size), `F0800_SAVEGAME_PC34ValidateGameCode_Compat(expectedGameCode, requireManifest)` (the per-game compatibility proof — strict mode rejects vanilla files, lenient mode accepts them for ReDMCSB interop), and `F0801_SAVEGAME_PC34GameCodeName_Compat` (stable ASCII names: DM1/CSB/DM2/NEXUS/THERON/UNSET/UNKNOWN). The importer stamps the parsed gameCode into the Firestaff `SaveGameHeader_Compat.reserved[5..6]` slot next to the existing GameID/MusicOn bytes, so the M12 launcher can quote the per-game verdict without re-parsing the PC 3.4 header. The CTest `test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` (data-free, previously dormant in the tree) was registered in `CMakeLists.txt` and extended from 6 to 14 invariants: `cpsc_obfuscate_reversible` (F0417 reversible XOR), `header_round_trip` (F0795 + F0796 byte-stable), `bad_inputs_rejected` (NULL state, NULL outBuf, NULL party, small outBuf, short buf, NULL outState), `cpsc_layout` (header + 5 parts, LENGTH prefixes), `error_string_lookup` (F0797 string dispatch for both LSV-01 and LSV-02 codes), `format_id_tolerance` (vanilla PC 3.4 byte layout preserved), and eight new LSV-02 cases — `lsv02_manifest_present_and_valid`, `lsv02_per_game_gate_accepts_dm1`, `lsv02_per_game_gate_rejects_wrong_game` (hand-crafts a CSB manifest to prove the F0796 + F0800 verdict), `lsv02_vanilla_fallback` (zero-padded buffer + lenient/strict gate), `lsv02_magic_tampering` (zeroes the LSV01RDM magic in-place and re-obfuscates, asserts NOT_PRESENT), `lsv02_import_stamps_reserved_gamecode` (round-trip populates reserved[5..6] + DM1 gate OK), `lsv02_export_byte_stable` (two consecutive exports with the same input produce identical bytes; divergent gameID changes the bytes), and `lsv02_game_code_name_lookup`. Source-locked against ReDMCSB DEFS.H:468-480 (DM_SAVE_HEADER.GameID), DEFS.H:538-572 (GLOBAL_DATA.MusicOn), LOADSAVE.C F0433/F0435 (save/load chain), SAVEHEAD.C F0429/F0430 (header read/write with the C10_DM_SAVE_HEADER_DECRYPTION_KEY_INDEX obfuscation), READWRIT.C F0417 (CPSC checksum + reversible obfuscate), and the existing `memory_savegame_pc34_compat.h:227` (RDMCSB15 native magic). Disjoint from the existing `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary_pc34_compat` (which gates the CSBWin dmsave/csbgame.dat path on 512-byte XOR/CSBWin 14-shape contract) and from the Theron `.srm` classifier (gzipped-deflate Save Disk manifest). Verification: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` clean configure, `cmake --build build --target test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat --parallel` clean, `gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -Iinclude -c src/memory/memory_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat.c` clean, `gcc -std=c99 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -O2 -Iinclude -c tests/test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat.c` clean, direct `./build/test_dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` PASS 14/14 (6 LSV-01 + 8 LSV-02), focused CTest `dm1_v1_savegame_pc34_native_export_pc34_compat` PASS 1/1, broader save/export/import CTest sweep (`savegame|save_browser|dm1_v1_savegame`) PASS 30/30 (no regressions in `save_browser_export_import_m12`, `dm1_v1_save_load_source_lock`, `pass607_dm1_v1_level_change_autosave_absence_source_lock`, `dm1_v1_save_load_slot_core`, `nexus_v1_save_slot_roundtrip_pc34_compat`, `nexus_v1_save_multislot_roundtrip_pc34_compat`, `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary_pc34_compat_unit`, `csb_v1_csbwin_save_loader_boundary`, `nexus_v1_save_load_round_trip`, `theron_v1_save_load`, `theron_v1_save_header_rejection`, `theron_v1_save_progress_roundtrip_pc34`, `pass789_dm1_v1_mirror_candidate_c040_save_game_while_panel_live`), tier1 CTest sweep PASS 10/10, full project `cmake --build build` clean, `git diff --check` clean. - ✅ 2026-06-28 M12 launcher cloud-sync opt-in boundary (gapbug_20260628_launcher_cloud_sync_boundary): bounded the existing `cloud_sync_m12` directory-based sync layer with an explicit launcher-owned opt-in gate and a conflict-safe no-op surface. The header now declares `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED` (clean return when opted out) and `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` (sync root missing / not a directory / not writable), plus `M12_CloudSync_SetEnabled/IsEnabled`, `M12_CloudSync_IsSyncRootUsable`, `M12_CloudSync_GetBoundaryTag` (stable tags `DISABLED` / `ENABLED_OK` / `ENABLED_NO_ROOT` / `ENABLED_NOT_A_DIR` / `ENABLED_UNWRITABLE`), and `M12_CloudSync_RunIfEnabled`. The implementation now: (1) defaults the opt-in flag to 0 (off) so the launcher is the single source of truth, (2) refuses bare relative paths and validates the sync root with `stat() + S_ISDIR + access(W_OK)` on every boundary check, (3) `RunIfEnabled` short-circuits to `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED` when off and to `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` when the root is unusable, never opening the manifest or touching tracked files, (4) `M12_CloudSync_ApplyConfig(const M12_Config*)` is the bounded wiring point that pushes `cloudSyncEnabled` + `cloudSyncDir` + `cloudSyncPolicy` into the runtime in one call, and (5) the existing `m12_apply_loaded_config` in `src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c` calls it right next to the `M11_HighContrast_SetActive` push so the boundary is hot on every launcher start. `M12_CloudSync_DiscoverSaveFiles(relativePrefix, absoluteDir)` now does a real bounded per-game `*.sav` directory walk (POSIX `opendir`/Win32 `FindFirstFile`, one level, `*.sav` only, idempotent on re-runs) and `m12_discover_tracked` calls it for `saves/{dm1,csb,dm2,nexus,theron}` instead of stubbing. The probe `probes/m12/firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe.c` was registered as CTest `m12_cloud_sync_boundary` and extended from 9 to 38 invariants covering: opt-in defaults disabled, `RunIfEnabled` is a strict no-op when off (no manifest file, zeroed stats, `M12_SYNC_OK_DISABLED`), `ENABLED_NOT_A_DIR` for a regular file, `ENABLED_NO_ROOT` after `rmdir`, `ENABLED_OK` for a valid dir, `M12_SYNC_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` from `RunIfEnabled` when the root is unusable, `ApplyConfig(NULL)` disables, `ApplyConfig` round-trips the flag + dir + policy, a re-disabled flag reverts the boundary at the next check, and `DiscoverSaveFiles` adds 2/2 `*.sav` entries, ignores `*.txt`, and is idempotent. Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe --parallel` clean, `gcc -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wno-format-truncation -Iinclude -Isrc -c probes/m12/firestaff_m12_cloud_sync_probe.c` clean, direct probe PASS 38/38, focused CTest `m12_cloud_sync_boundary` PASS 1/1, broader `m12_*` regression set PASS 11/12 with the single failure (`m12_polished_ui_flow`) confirmed pre-existing on `origin/main` via `git stash`, full project `cmake --build build` PASS, `git diff --check` clean. Honest scope: launcher/settings + runtime boundary only — directory-based sync model, no real cloud provider, no `m12_save_browser_export_import` payload movement, no README claim, and no promotion of the `Cloud sync` row in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` from `OPEN-LARGE` (real cloud provider integration, multi-device encryption, conflict resolution UI, and push/pull scheduling remain open).

- ✅ 2026-06-28 runtime gesture navigation gate (input translation + touch target safety): added `runtime_gesture_navigation_gate` module (`include/runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.h` + `src/engine/runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.c`) plus data-free CTest unit `tests/test_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate.c` (15 invariant groups, 50+ PASS) and headless CI probe `probes/m11/firestaff_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate_probe.c` (9 groups + 50-iteration determinism, status=PASS). The gate is the deterministic cross-game contract behind the existing `firestaff_touch.c` swipe + edge-strafe primitives: `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_Evaluate(event, policy, result)` consumes a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavEvent` (framebuffer-space start/end coords + threshold/tolerance) and a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavPolicy` (`accessibilityTouchEnabled`, `v2PresentationEnabled`, `v1ParityPreserve`) and returns a `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNavDecision` + `FS_Command` code mapped to the existing `FS_CMD_*` enum (`FS_CMD_MOVE_FORWARD=1 / _MOVE_BACKWARD=2 / _TURN_LEFT=3 / _TURN_RIGHT=4 / _STRAFE_LEFT=5 / _STRAFE_RIGHT=6`) so callers can index a single integer. Swipe up/down/left/right map to move_forward / move_backward / turn_left / turn_right (cross-V1/V2 path - the same FS_Command codes the V1 keyboard path already consumes via `fs_input_queue_push`); edge-left/right map to strafe_left / strafe_right and are V2-only with `v1ParityPreserve` + `v2PresentationEnabled` guard. The gate rejects six boundary cases: `rejected_disabled` (touch setting off), `rejected_too_short` (travel below `FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_SWIPE_THRESHOLD_PX=40` or below the caller's `tapTolerancePx<=FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_TAP_TOLERANCE_PX=24` tap-tolerance guard), `rejected_too_small_target` (edge zone narrower than the 44 px Apple HIG / WCAG 2.5.5 floor pinned by `RUNTIME_GESTURE_NAV_MIN_TARGET_PX`), `rejected_ambiguous` (diagonal swipe with equal horizontal/vertical axis), `rejected_null` (NULL event/policy safety), and `rejected_v1_only` (V2 edge-strafe called when `v2PresentationEnabled=0` or `v1ParityPreserve=1`). `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_TouchTargetSafe(w, h)` is the touch-target safety contract (returns 1 when both axes >= 44 px, 0 when either is negative or below floor) and `FirestaffRuntimeGestureNav_SourceViewportSafe(sourceW, sourceH, surfaceW, surfaceH)` extends the floor to source-viewport scale safety (the 320x200 source framebuffer's shortest axis must scale to >= 44 px on the running surface). Source-locked against ReDMCSB `COMMAND.C:2045-2155 F0380_COMMAND_ProcessQueue_CPSC` (movement/turn queue dispatch that consumes the same C001..C006 movement IDs), `CLIKMENU.C:142-174 F0365 turn` (turn dispatch), `CLIKMENU.C:180-390 F0366 move` (step dispatch), `GAMELOOP.C:164-219 V1 input wait loop` (V1 parity surface), `DEFS.H:238-243 C001..C006 movement commands`, `DEFS.H:197-211 C003/C005 strafe owner`, `src/engine/firestaff_touch.c FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_SWIPE_THRESHOLD_PX=40 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_TAP_TOLERANCE_PX=24 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_LONG_PRESS_MS=500 / FIRESTAFF_TOUCH_EDGE_ZONE_FRAC=0.20`, `src/dm1v2/dm1_v2_touch_controller_affordance_pc34.c DM1_V2_AFFORDANCE_TOUCH_EDGE_STRAFE_LEFT/RIGHT` (V2-only edge-strafe affordance enumeration), and `include/config_m12.h dm1V2AccessibilityTouchEnabled` (the launcher setting that gates the whole contract). Touch-target floor 44 px documented as Apple HIG 44x44 pt + Material Design 48 dp + WCAG 2.5.5 44 px / iOS HIG, the smallest documented recommendation the gate must respect on a 320x200 source viewport. Disjoint from `firestaff_touch.c` (which owns the SDL-touch-event-driven swipe detection primitives), from `touch_pointer_input_pc34_compat.c` (which owns the screen-letterbox touch-pointer dispatch into the DM1 input command queue), from `dm1_v2_touch_controller_affordance_pc34.c` (which owns the V2-only affordance enumeration + adapter), from the DM1/CSB/DM2/Nexus `*_v2_touch_controller_affordance` siblings (per-game V2 affordance tables), and from the per-game `*_v2_touch_runtime` runtime bridges (V1->V2 input pipeline wire-ups). Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate firestaff_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate_probe --parallel` clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2` (no new warnings), direct `./build/test_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate` PASS 50+ assertions across all 15 invariant groups (failures=0), direct `./build/firestaff_runtime_gesture_navigation_gate_probe` PASS all 9 groups + 50-iteration determinism (status=PASS), focused `ctest --test-dir build -R '^runtime_gesture_navigation_gate$|^runtime_gesture_navigation_gate_probe$' --output-on-failure` PASS 2/2, broader touch + session_timer + V2-touch affordance regression set PASS 28/28 (no regressions in `touch_pointer_input_pc34_compat`, `touch_item_mouse_queue_pc34_compat`, `touch_movement_turn_routes_pc34_compat`, `touch_click_zone_matrix_pc34_compat`, `m11_touch_pointer_dispatch_probe`, `pass491_touch_pointer_mouse_queue_runtime_gate`, `m12_session_timer`, `campaign_m12_session_timer`, `session_timer_runtime`, `touch_movement_viewport_source_lock`, `dm1_v1_touch_input_source_locked_ui_zones`, `dm1_v1_wall_click_touch_seam_source_lock`, `dm1_v2_touch_controller_affordance_pc34`, `csb_v2_touch_controller_affordance`, `dm1_v2_touch_controller_affordance_source_lock`, `nexus_v2_touch_controller_affordance`), `git diff --check` clean, `cmake --build build` (full project) clean exit code 0. - ✅ 2026-06-27 Theron V1 SRM progression-envelope readiness gate: extended the bounded Save Disk `.srm` classifier with `theron_v1_srm_decode_progression_payload()`, a Firestaff-only inflated-body envelope that restores a between-dungeon checkpoint into `Theron_DungeonProgression` through the existing restore API. The 44-byte body carries magic/version, current dungeon, 7-bit quest-item mask, current level, playtime, and seven little-endian dungeon seeds; the decoder validates the THQUEST.ASM T080/T800 sequence rule that completed quest bits must form a prefix and the save must point at the next dungeon (or dungeon 7 for all-complete). The SRM unit test and probe now inflate a synthetic gzip stream to this body and assert the restored dungeon-3 checkpoint (`quest_items=0x03`, dungeons 1-2 COMPLETE, dungeon 3 AVAILABLE, seeds 0x1001..0x1007). Verification: built `test_theron_v1_srm_classifier_pc34` and `firestaff_theron_v1_srm_classifier_probe`; focused CTest `theron_v1_srm_classifier|theron_v1_srm_classifier_probe` PASS 2/2. - ✅ 2026-06-26 DM1 V1 Hall of Champions inscription readability fix: restored the ReDMCSB readable-inscription path for front-wall HoC text. M11 now loads only the real `WallOrnamentCount` bytes from DUNGEON.DAT metadata and then sets the synthetic inscription wall-ornament slot to `C0_WALL_ORNAMENT_INSCRIPTION` in memory, matching ReDMCSB `DUNGEON.C F0173` lines 2758-2762 instead of reading a bogus file byte such as `254` into that slot. The runtime inscription detector now compares the square aspect against the local synthetic inscription slot from `DUNGEON.C F0172/F0174` lines 2585-2593, then maps that local slot to global ornament 0 for drawing. The D1C readable text renderer also restores the ReDMCSB `DUNVIEW.C F0107` wall patch (`M712_NEGGRAPHIC_`/`C735`, lines 3679-3682) before blitting M648 inscription glyphs (lines 3697-3706), so Hall text is not drawn directly over noisy wall stone. Added `firestaff_dm1_v1_hoc_inscription_readability_runtime_probe`, which opens real DM1 data, finds a real visible HoC wall TextString (`THIS WALL SAYS` / `NOTHING` on the local PC 3.4 data), proves the synthetic slot maps to global inscription ornament 0, and requires black/dark patch rows plus visible M648 glyph pixels. Verification: built `firestaff`, the new HoC inscription probe, `firestaff_m11_inscription_font_probe`, `firestaff_m11_v1_nearest_cpu_present_probe`, and `firestaff_m11_phase_a_probe`; direct probes PASS; focused CTest `hoc_inscription|m11_inscription_font|m11_v1_nearest_cpu_present_probe|m11_phase_a` PASS 4/4.

- ✅ 2026-06-26 X68000 HDM real-media receipt + cross-module FTL-handoff gates: added `probes/x68k/firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus_probe.c` (skip-safe CTest `firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus`, 10/10 PASS) and `probes/x68k/firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus_probe.c` (skip-safe CTest `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus`, 8/8 PASS) on top of the existing data-free `firestaff_x68k_media_classify_unit` (12/12) and synthetic-FTL `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_unit` (5/5). The new receipt probe verifies the DMWeb-documented 2DHD X68000 geometry and protection-sector surface against the local public DMFiles DM1 X68000 v3.0 HDM `~/.firestaff/data/dm1-extras/x68000-3.0-jp/DungeonMasterX68000version30Japanese.hdm` (1,261,568 bytes, exact DMWeb `2 sides * 77 tracks * 8 sectors * 1024 bytes`): full-disk class, no FTL 0x6160 magic at offset 0, Hudson Soft boot block at offset 0 (`60 1c ...`), 1024/1024 `0xE5E5...` MFM-fill bytes in the DMWeb-documented Track 1 Side 1 Sector 9 region (the documented public-DMFiles state, which lacks the protection sector), no `HPR-0007` sentinel at the DMWeb-documented sector-9 linear offset (so a future re-issued master that puts one there will flip this receipt to FAIL with a clear diff), `IsUnprotectedDisk == 0` because the protection region is MFM fill not zero, and `IsFTLPayload == 0` because the HDM starts with the Hudson Soft boot block. The new handoff probe scans the same real HDM for embedded FTL resources via `FirestaffFtlContainer_Parse` (greatstone `d_ftl.html` common-header magic 0x6160 big-endian, hunk_count at offset 18) and finds **2 parseable FTL containers** at offsets 73,728 (0x12000) and 460,800 (0x70800); the first FTL's BSS `data_area1_memory_size` (24,720 bytes) is verified to fit the on-disk HDM media class via `FirestaffX68kMedia_FTLHandoffFits`, and the helper's documented boundary cases are cross-checked on the real media (`size+1` reject, `0` accept as size-unknown, `disk_bytes` accept). Source of truth: dmweb-free.fr/community/documentation/copy-protection "Sharp X68000" section (2DHD geometry, `HPR-0007` sentinel, MFM no-flux-area), dmweb DM X68000 edition page (HDM original image that cannot boot without protection sectors), greatstone `d_ftl.html` "20-byte common header" magic 0x6160 BE and Note 7 handoff math, the existing `include/firestaff_x68k_media_classify.h` (constants, scan flags, FTLHandoffFits) and `include/firestaff_ftl_container.h` (parser contract). **Known limitation surfaced:** the classifier's `ftl_magic_candidate_count` field scans only the first 32 KiB (per its documented contract for single-resource `.FTL` payloads) but the real DMFiles X68000 HDM embeds FTL resources at offsets > 32 KiB, so the candidate-count field reads 0 even though the full-HDM scan finds 2 parseable FTL containers. The receipt explicitly surfaces both numbers as notes (`classifier ftl_magic_candidate_count (first 32 KiB) = 0; full-HDM parseable FTL count = 2`) rather than asserting a false-positive guarantee. Disjoint from the data-free `firestaff_x68k_media_classify_unit` (which stays data-free so CI runs without real media) and the synthetic-FTL `firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_unit` (which validates the handoff math against an in-memory synthetic FTL container). Skip-safe: hosts without a known DM1 X68000 HDM exit 0 with a SKIP message on both probes. The probes do NOT vend game data, do NOT parse MFM flux timing, do NOT claim original-vs-cracked-vs-save-disk authenticity (the off-axis `HPR-0007` strings embedded in `B:\\DMGame.bak` backup labels are surfaced as a separate finding for the TODO follow-up), do NOT provide 31 kHz presentation evidence, and do NOT cover X68000 keypad/arrow input gates or emulator/runtime launch proof — those remain tracked in `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` and the `TODO.md` 2026-06-25 row. Verification: `cmake -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DBUILD_TESTING=ON`, `cmake --build build --target firestaff_x68k_media_receipt_real_corpus_probe firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff_real_corpus_probe test_firestaff_x68k_media_classify test_firestaff_x68k_ftl_handoff --parallel 4` clean (no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra -pedantic -O2`), strict CI `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -Wno-format-truncation -std=c99` clean on both new probe sources, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^firestaff_x68k_' --output-on-failure` PASS 4/4 (data-free classifier + synthetic-FTL handoff + real-media receipt + real-media FTL handoff), focused regression set `ctest -R '^(firestaff_x68k_|firestaff_ftl_container_unit|firestaff_ftl_hunk_data_zero_run_unit)'` PASS 6/6, `tools/asset-validate/no_game_data_in_git.py` PASS, `git diff --check HEAD` clean. Default probe path: `~/.firestaff/data/dm1-extras/x68000-3.0-jp/DungeonMasterX68000version30Japanese.hdm` (operator can override via `FIRESTAFF_X68K_HDM_PATH=<path>`); the DMFiles English DIM is intentionally not in the default candidate list (256-byte DIM header changes the on-disk byte alignment and would fail the size receipt honestly).

- ✅ 2026-06-26 CSB Hint Oracle UI/runtime binding gate: added `csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding` (include + src/csb) on top of the existing `csb_hint_oracle_htc` format-contract parser and the `csb_hint_oracle_htc_real_scan` real-asset scan/cache. The new module exposes three runtime-adjacent binding surfaces that prove a decoded HCSB.HTC page or page-slice can reach a Firestaff-facing oracle/hint surface (a printable text/buffer the launcher or M11 view can render): `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_format_report()` writes a multi-line diagnostic/oracle report (matched MD5 + label, file size, resolved path, format word + dungeon id, location/hint/page counts, the hint 0 first-page binding smoke, and the level=0 (255, 255) wildcard binding smoke); `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_format_hint(hint_index)` writes the hint name + first-page decoded text for any hint; `csb_hint_oracle_ui_binding_resolve_location(level, x, y)` resolves a (level, x, y) into the first matching hint's name + first-page decoded text. Source-locked: ReDMCSB `HINTLOAD.C:11-18`, `HINTHTC.C:177-358`, `HINTLZW.C:122-212`, plus dmweb Hint Oracle Files page. The binding surface is intentionally small: it does not draw a graphical Hint Oracle overlay, it does not bind into the M11 game loop or M12 launch flow, and it does not claim parity for every Utility Disk release variant — the known-hash list in `csb_hint_oracle_htc_real_scan` still gates which HCSB.HTCs we accept; the binding surface itself is variant-agnostic. CTest-gated as `csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_unit` (data-free, synthetic in-memory fixture, 6/6 invariants PASS: not-loaded argument handling, report contains the binding smoke (matched MD5/label + format word + dungeon id + counts + hint 0 first-page text "Cast/ZOKATHRA" + wildcard resolve surface), format_hint round-trip, resolve_location binding (level=5 (255,255) → hint 1 "ANYWHERE" + first-page text "Anywhere"), truncation path, result-name table) and `csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding` (real-asset, `firestaff_csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_probe.c`, labels `tier2;csb;hint_oracle;real_data;skip_safe`, 32/32 invariants PASS). End-to-end on the local Atari ST 2.x HCSB.HTC (md5 `8ce69b54cf255a15e98e909bb45b9742`, 66,172 bytes): binding report surfaces the matched MD5/label + format word 2 + dungeon id 13 + the parsed location/hint/page counts; `format_hint(0)` writes the hint 0 "FULYA PIT" header + the parsed first-page text starting `"This is where Lord Chaos mined the deadly Mana-absorbing Corbum.."` (printable ASCII, full text round-trips); `resolve_location(level=0, 255, 255)` resolves to hint 197 "CREATURES" and writes the first-page text starting `"Learn well the shapes and forms dread Chaos make"` (the binding surface reaches a real decoded HCSB.HTC page on the verified Utility Disk HCSB.HTC); second scan + binding is byte-identical to the first (deterministic); out-of-range hint index and non-matching (level, x, y) tuples return the documented error codes with empty buffers; `(not loaded)` is written when the cache is empty. Disjoint from `csb_hint_oracle_htc_unit` (data-free parser) and from `csb_v1_hint_oracle_real_htc_scan` (scan/cache); the binding surface reuses both. Verification: `cmake --build build --target firestaff_csb_v1_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding_probe test_csb_hint_oracle_ui_runtime_binding`, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^hint_oracle' --output-on-failure` PASS 4/4 (data-free parser + data-free binding + real-asset scan + real-asset binding), strict `-Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic` clean on probe + test + binding source, `tools/asset-validate/no_game_data_in_git.py` PASS, `git diff --check HEAD` clean. - ✅ 2026-06-25 FM Towns BIN/CUE and ISO/CUE redump-layout classifier: added `firestaff_fmtowns_cd_classify` (include + src/shared) implementing a bounded CUE-sheet parser for the FM Towns DM1 v2.0, CSB v3.1, and DM2 v1.0 CD-image lines. Source-of-truth: docs/DMWEB_REFERENCE.md lines 37 (DM1 FM Towns: redump BIN/CUE masters T1/T2 + ISO/CUE archive, audio tracks 02..20 with 04/07/20 unused and track 20 silent), 44 (CSB FM Towns: redump BIN/CUE archive, audio tracks 02..31), and 51 (DM2 FM Towns: redump BIN/CUE image, quieter tracks 2..6 + silent track 8). The classifier parses redump-style CUE sheets in memory (FILE/TRACK/INDEX/PREGAP/REM/CATALOG), distinguishes MODE1/2352 vs MODE1/2048 vs AUDIO tracks, optionally reads a 6-byte ISO 9660 PVD signature (`\x01CD001`) at the standard data-track byte offset (sector 16, byte 1), and scores the disc against the documented DMWeb CD-audio track tables for DM1 (17..19 audio), CSB (28..30 audio), and DM2 (5..7 audio + silent track 8). Wired into CTest as `firestaff_fmtowns_cd_classify_unit` with 16/16 internal cases: DM1 20-track layout, CSB 31-track layout, DM2 8-track layout, single-file ISO MODE1/2048 layout, all-audio-disc rejection, TRACK-before-FILE rejection, unterminated FILE quote rejection, single-audio-disc returns `GAME_NONE`, synthetic ISO 9660 PVD detection (positive and corrupted), LF-only line endings tolerated, REM/';' comments tolerated, PREGAP/INDEX 00 marker tolerated. Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_firestaff_fmtowns_cd_classify` clean (no warnings under `-Wall -Wextra -pedantic -O2`), direct probe PASS, `ctest --test-dir build -R '^firestaff_fmtowns_cd_classify_unit$'` PASS 1/1, focused regression set `ctest -R '^(firestaff_fmtowns_cd_classify_unit|firestaff_amg_decode_unit|firestaff_pak_decode_unit|firestaff_cmp_decode_unit|firestaff_img5_decode_unit|firestaff_ftl_container_unit|firestaff_ftl_hunk_data_zero_run_unit|firestaff_sck_mapfile)$'` PASS 8/8, and `git diff --check` clean. Stays bounded: does NOT extract ISO 9660 file payloads, does NOT decode IMG2/GRAPHICS.DAT/DUNGEON.DAT, does NOT launch any FM Towns emulator, and does NOT vendor or hash any game data — those gates remain on `docs/FIRESTAFF_GAP_LIST.md` as `OPEN-BOUNDED`. The DM1 FM Towns row of the gap list is now annotated `OPEN-BOUNDED / PARTIAL-EVIDENCE` to record the classifier without promoting the row to FIXED.

The fixture synthesizes a single ZIP whose graphics entry sits at the deeply-nested path `nested/inner/level1/level2/DM2GRAPHICS.DAT` and whose dungeon entry is flat; both are deflated (method=8) when zlib is available so the deflate stream is strictly smaller than the source payload (the inflate code path is what is actually exercised, not a stored-entry fallback). CMake `pkg_check_modules(ZLIB)` now drives `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB` (default OFF) so the test gets `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB=1` plus `PkgConfig::ZLIB` on hosts with zlib, and falls back to stored entries otherwise. Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate` clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2`, focused CTest PASS, and `asset_find_by_hash` / `dm1_pc34_multilanguage_required_gate` / asset-cache CTests all still PASS. - ✅ 2026-06-22 Nested deflated ZIP entry → asset-cache materialization regression: added `tests/test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate.c` and registered it as CTest target `asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate`. The fixture synthesizes a single ZIP whose graphics entry sits at the deeply-nested path `nested/inner/level1/level2/DM2GRAPHICS.DAT` and whose dungeon entry is flat; both are deflated (method=8) when zlib is available so the deflate stream is strictly smaller than the source payload (the inflate code path is what is actually exercised, not a stored-entry fallback). The gate proves three layers end-to-end: (1) the recursive hash scanner reports the match as a virtual path `<zip>::<nested/.../ENTRY>` and preserves every path segment of the nested entry name; (2) the low-level `asset_extract_virtual_path()` helper inflates the deflate stream and writes a byte-identical ordinary file; (3) the M12 cache materializer rewrites both required-file matched paths to ordinary files under `<userDataDir>/asset-cache/dm2/{GRAPHICS,DUNGEON}.DAT` so the runtime never has to understand virtual container paths. CMake `pkg_check_modules(ZLIB)` now drives `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB` (default OFF) so the test gets `FIRESTAFF_HAS_ZLIB=1` plus `PkgConfig::ZLIB` on hosts with zlib, and falls back to stored entries otherwise. Verification: `cmake --build build --target test_asset_status_zip_cache_nested_deflate` clean with `-Wall -Wextra -O2`, focused CTest PASS, and `asset_find_by_hash` / `dm1_pc34_multilanguage_required_gate` / asset-cache CTests all still PASS. Source-locked against `src/shared/asset_find_by_hash.c` (zip_stored_entry_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_md5 / scan_zip_by_md5 / zip_deflated_entry_extract / asset_extract_virtual_path) and `src/shared/asset_status_m12.c` (m12_path_is_virtual_asset / m12_materialize_required_file / m12_materialize_runtime_cache_for_game). This is a cache-handoff contract regression only; it does not claim original capture parity, real CSB/DM2 launch paths, or pixel evidence.

- ✅ 2026-06-28 Launcher session timer runtime overlay: landed the in-game handoff boundary for the launcher-owned Session Timer setting (`Off` / `15m` / `30m` / `60m` / `120m`) so the M11 game view now consults the persisted limit during gameplay and surfaces a deterministic reminder overlay + forced-pause confirm dialog instead of silently running past the user's chosen cap. New module `src/shared/session_timer_runtime.c` + header `include/session_timer_runtime.h` owns the runtime state machine: `SessionTimerRuntime_Init(limitMinutes)` seeds the limit, `SessionTimerRuntime_Tick(seconds)` accumulates elapsed seconds, `SessionTimerRuntime_Poll()` reports one of three events (`SESSION_TIMER_RUNTIME_EVENT_RUNNING`, `_EVENT_REMINDER_DUE`, `_EVENT_FORCED_PAUSE`), `SessionTimerRuntime_Acknowledge()` clears the pending reminder latch + re-arms the next window, `SessionTimerRuntime_ClearForcedPause()` releases the latch, and `SessionTimerRuntime_FormatRemaining(buf, size)` writes `HH:MM:SS` / `Off`. The reminder threshold + re-arm window default to 300 s (5 min) and are documented constants, not ReDMCSB-derived. Off-mode + negative ticks + post-limit ticks + null-pointer inputs are all safe no-ops; pre-arm at init when `limitSeconds <= reminderThresholdSeconds` so a 1-min limit surfaces the reminder up front. M11 wire-up: `include/m11_game_view.h` adds `sessionTimerRuntime` + `sessionTimerForcedPauseDialogActive` + `sessionTimerReminderOverlayActive` fields, and the `M11_GameView_InitFromMenuSessionTimer / Tick / Acknowledge / ClearForcedPause / GetForcedPauseDialogActive / GetReminderOverlayActive` API; `M11_GameView_OpenSelectedMenuEntry` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:7169-7170) seeds the runtime from `M12_StartupMenu_SessionTimerLimitMinutes(menuState)` at every game launch and the CSB/Theron V2 settings bridge keeps its existing branch; `M11_GameView_Draw` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:~28310) paints the reminder banner (200x14 yellow-on-black top strip with `SESSION TIMER HH:MM:SS REMAINING`) and the forced-pause confirm dialog (240x60 dimmed-centered box with `SESSION TIMER EXPIRED (HH:MM:SS) -- RETURN TO MENU` + `PRESS ENTER TO RETURN TO MENU` / `ESC TO DISMISS`); `M11_GameView_HandleInput` (src/engine/m11_game_view.c:~8430) gates ACCEPT/ACTION on the forced-pause dialog to return-to-launcher and BACK to dismiss-and-resume, and any non-NONE input dismisses the reminder banner; `M11_GameView_Shutdown` / `_Init` keep the same memset-zero contract so the runtime is freshly seeded at every launch (no leftover FORCED_PAUSE latch from a previous run). The main loop in `src/engine/main_loop_m11.c:2720-2735` ticks the runtime once per >=1 s of active gameplay via `M11_GameView_TickSessionTimer(&gameView, loopDeltaMs/1000)` and lets the runtime's Off-mode + post-limit no-op semantics keep the loop safe even when the user has the timer set to Off. The runtime is a Firestaff UX boundary — there is no original DM1/CSB/DM2/Nexus/Theron title-screen timer on PC 3.4 to source-lock against, and no ReDMCSB line numbers are cited because no gameplay behavior is touched. Verification: new CTest target `session_timer_runtime` (tests/test_session_timer_runtime.c, all-PASS) covers Off-mode, 60-min boundary math, REMINDER_DUE latch + Acknowledge re-arm, FORCED_PAUSE latch + ClearForcedPause, post-clear re-latch on a 1s tick, Reset preserves limit, FormatRemaining for Off/HH:MM:SS/null/zero-buffer, default-exposure sanity, null-pointer tolerance, and the 1-min limit immediate reminder pre-arm; new CTest target `session_timer_runtime_probe` (probes/runtime/firestaff_session_timer_runtime_probe.c, all-PASS 12/12) covers the M11/M12 hand-off smoke (launcher Off-mode -> runtime Off-mode, 60-min runtime surfaces REMINDER_DUE at the 55-min boundary with the documented 300 s threshold, Acknowledge + 60 s tick stays in RUNNING within the re-arm window, 60-min runtime surfaces FORCED_PAUSE at the limit, FormatRemaining matches `M12_StartupMenu_SessionTimerRemainingSeconds`, `M12_CampaignSessionTimer` flushes into slot independent of runtime state, ClearForcedPause + zero-tick leaves runtime in RUNNING, 15-min limit reports RUNNING while 1-min limit reports REMINDER_DUE at init, Reset returns to RUNNING with full limit, launcher round-trip across 0/15/30/60/120 minutes stays coherent, default reminder + re-arm window = 300 s); the existing `m12_session_timer`, `campaign_m12_session_timer`, `m12_startup_menu`, `m12_menu_mouse`, `m12_language_cycle_layout`, `m11_phase_a`, `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat`, `m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe`, `m12_launcher_screen_reader_manifest`, and `firestaff_accessibility_manifest_unit` all still PASS; - ✅ 2026-06-22 Theron V1 save/load progress round-trip regression: new `test_theron_v1_save_progress_roundtrip_pc34` data-free CTest target packs a real Theron_V1_Party (Theron + Mara + Vey + Ruk, mid-Crypt-of-Shadows, item reset applied, gold 4321, second quest item set) through `theron_v1_party_pack` into the slot champion stream, writes slot 4 via `theron_v1_save_to_slot`, reads it back via `theron_v1_save_load_from_slot`, and unpacks via `theron_v1_party_unpack`. Every documented `Theron_V1_Champion` field (name, health/max, mana/max, stamina/max, stats, skill levels, wounds, alive flag, primary_class, portrait_index, inventory slots, equipment slots, food/water) is asserted byte-equal across the round-trip plus the parallel `Theron_DungeonProgression` invariants (current_dungeon/level, dungeon_states, quest_items_collected/in_current_dungeon, item_reset_mode/applied, dungeon_playtime_seconds, seeds). A re-save overwrite round-trip locks slot-hygiene (no stale-tail/partial-write). The regression test caught a real bug: `theron_v1_save_load_from_slot` returned `Theron_SaveSlot.slot_index = 0` regardless of the slot the caller asked for, because `parse_save_image` memsets the struct before extracting file bytes and `load_from_slot` never re-pinned the slot index. Mirroring the existing `theron_v1_save_import_slot` post-parse assignment now lets callers cross-check the slot they just loaded against the metadata they receive. Verification: direct binary PASS, focused Theron CTest sweep 31/31 green (no regressions), and broader `save_load|theron|tier1|tier2|tier4|v1-compatibility|v1` sweep 22/22 green. Source-locked against `include/theron_v1_save_load.h` (slotN.tqsv layout), `include/theron_v1_champions.h` (Theron_V1_Party + Theron_V1_Champion), `include/theron_v1_dungeon_progression.h`, THQUEST.ASM T080 (between-dungeon save/load), and THQUEST.ASM T800 (champion persistence between dungeons). Disjoint from `test_theron_v1_save_load` (dummy champion bytes) and `test_theron_v1_save_header_rejection` (mutated single header bytes). Documented in-file: map-level fields (`leader_x`/`leader_y`/`leader_dir`/`levitating`/`door_state_override`/`gold`) live in `Theron_V1_Party` outside the 4×`Theron_V1_Champion` pack stream and are not preserved by the current pack/unpack path; the test pins that documented behavior so a future struct-shape regression cannot silently start writing them into the pack stream without flagging the change.

- ✅ 2026-06-29 DM1 V1 post-dungeon reviewed-target-selection hardness: the runbook Step 5b.1 selection step is now a real accountability gate. **Contract:** new `docs/parity/DM1_V1_POST_DUNGEON_PAIRING_TARGET_CONTRACT.json` (schema `firestaff.dm1_v1.post_dungeon_pairing_target_contract.v1`) pins the five supported target kinds (`creature_chain` / `champion_panel` / `wall_door_fakewall` / `viewport` / `collision`) with source anchors (DUNVIEW.C F0097/F0115/F0128, CLIKMENU.C F0366, CLIKVIEW.C F0377, MOVESENS.C F0267, CHAMDRAW.C F0296, OBJECT.C F0038, plus G0219/G0221/G0222 creature aspect/palette tables from the existing creature-chain contract), per-kind `minimumRouteSteps`, per-kind `requiredSelectionFields`, per-kind `minimumSemanticChecks`, the canonical 10 PASS_IDs (`pass1052`..`pass1072`), and the three baseline non_claim entries. **Validator:** new `docs/parity/tools/dm1_v1_post_dungeon_pairing_target_selector.py` is the runnable companion; it refuses to write `target_selection.receipt.json` until 12 pin checks all PASS (target_kind supported; reviewer_name + reviewer_run_id safe against a conservative character class; reviewer_pass_id in the contract's 10 known PASS_IDs; selection_rationale present; route_steps count >= kind minimum; every route_step.key in the live runner's `Keypad-2`/`Keypad-4`/`Keypad-5`/`Keypad-6`/`Keypad-8` set; expected_terminal_classifier_state matches the kind contract `dungeon_gameplay`; expected_terminal_sensor_family matches the kind contract family; non_claims contains the three baseline entries; asset_set DUNGEON.DAT + GRAPHICS.DAT matches the contract reference SHA256s; cited preflight receipt exists and every `pin_checks[i].status` is `PASS`). The selector ships a hermetic `--self-test` that covers 5 positive cases (one per supported kind) + 11 negative cases (unknown kind, empty reviewer, unknown PASS_ID, too-short route, unsupported key, missing required field, missing baseline non_claim, asset-set mismatch, preflight receipt missing, preflight pin violation, expected terminal classifier state mismatch); it does NOT launch DOSBox. **CTest wiring:** new `dm1_v1_post_dungeon_pairing_target_selector` CTest entry is added in `CMakeLists.txt` with `TIMEOUT 60`. **Runbook-consistency probe:** `tools/test_dm1_v1_capture_runbook_consistency.py` adds `post_dungeon_target_selector_selftest` which (a) runs the selector self-test, (b) introspects the selector's pinned SUPPORTED_ROUTE_KEYS set against the live runner's KEY_MAP (catches future drift), (c) verifies the three baseline non_claim entries are still present in the selector constant, (d) drives a synthetic negative CLI invocation with `pass9999` and asserts it is refused, and (e) drives a synthetic positive CLI invocation and asserts the receipt is written with the correct `firestaff.dm1_v1.post_dungeon_pairing_target_selection.v1` schema. The probe moves from 20/20 PASS to 21/21 PASS. **Runbook:** `docs/parity/DM1_V1_ORIGINAL_CAPTURE_RUNBOOK.md` Step 5b.1 is split into 5b.1 (the existing live receipt) and the new Step 5b.1.a (the reviewed-target-selection gate, required before any live post-dungeon route is dispatched). **Verification (2026-06-29):** selector self-test PASS (5 supported kinds, 11 negative cases); runbook-consistency probe 21/21 PASS; CTest entry wired in `CMakeLists.txt` `dm1_v1_post_dungeon_pairing_target_selector`. Local destructive probe (corrupted PASS marker in selector output) flips the probe to 20/21 FAIL with the precise `[post_dungeon_target_selector_selftest]` failure; local destructive probe (added `Keypad-3` to `SUPPORTED_ROUTE_KEYS` without updating the live runner's `KEY_MAP`) also flips the probe to 20/21 FAIL with the route-key drift message. **Non-claim:** the contract + selector are an accountability gate, not a parity promoter. They do not promote `B1` / `B3` capture-gap rows. Original-vs-Firestaff pixel diffs, creature screenshots, four-champion HUD screenshots, and I34E debugger rows stay BLOCKED or PARTIAL until paired artifacts exist. No proprietary game frames are touched, paired, or tracked.

### DM1 V2.0 / V2.1 / V2.2

- ✅ V2.0 filtered presentation: config, CRT scanlines, palette correction, dither cleanup, sharpening, renderer integration, and launcher/menu integration.
- ✅ DM1 V2.2 GPU render path per-frame shape cache: new `m11_v22_shape_cache_pc34` module (include + src) provides the data-flow seam between the V22 shape book (m11_v22_shape_for_cell) and the M11 per-cell draw passes. Module-static 3x3 cache (D1..D3, L/C/R) populated by `m11_v22_shape_cache_update(direction, raw_squares)` called from `m11_draw_viewport` after the sample loop, and consulted via `m11_v22_shape_cache_get(depth, lateral)` + `m11_v22_shape_cache_active(depth, lateral)`. The cache is in its own module so tests can link it without pulling in the full M11 game view + image frontend chain. ctest target `test_m11_v22_shape_cache_pc34` passes 23/23 (V1 default all-cells-inactive, V22 active all-9-cells-resolve, V1↔V22 transition, OOB depth/lateral, evidence). Headless probe `firestaff_m11_v22_shape_cache_probe` passes 17/17. Source-locked against ReDMCSB DUNVIEW.C:6697-6816 (composition draw order), DUNGEON.C:2238-2246 (square type decode), DEFS.H:922 (M034_SQUARE_TYPE).
- ✅ DM1 V2.2 GPU render path V22 modern-art overlay: new `m11_v22_render_overlay_pc34` module (include + src) completes the V22 dispatch by painting a placeholder colored rectangle over each V22-active cell on the V1 framebuffer. The placeholder is a filled rectangle (palette index derived from the V22 shape's color_tint RGB average) with a 1-pixel border using the fixed `M11_V22_OVERLAY_PLACEHOLDER_INDEX` (0xFF). Called from `m11_draw_viewport` after the V1 palette-apply pass and before the turn-pan pass. The V1 m11_draw_dm1_* draw passes are NOT modified (the overlay is layered on top of the V1 pixels, not swapped in-place). ctest target `test_m11_v22_render_overlay_pc34` passes 13/13 (V1 inactive = 0 cells painted + no pixels change, V22 active = 9 cells painted, 1-pixel border uses the placeholder index, NULL/zero framebuffer safe). Headless probe `firestaff_m11_v22_render_overlay_probe` passes 13/13. The real V22 modern art (PBR textures, normal maps, etc.) lives in `~/.firestaff/assets/dm1/modern/` and is a follow-up; this commit delivers the end-to-end V22 data flow: M12 menu -> V2 settings wire-up -> m11_v22_shape_cache_update -> m11_v22_render_overlay -> V1 framebuffer pixels. Source-locked against ReDMCSB DUNVIEW.C:6697-6816.

- ✅ CSB V2.1 texture upscale test+probe (9-square + panel + V22 EPX): `test_csb_v2_texture_upscale_pc34` and `firestaff_csb_v2_texture_upscale_probe` had pre-fix test bugs that made `t_epx_2x`, `t_9square_viewport`, `t_panel`, and `t_present_mode_v22_triggers_epx` (and the matching probe checks) fail when the source pattern starts with 0. The `epx_buf[0] != 0` check was wrong because EPX writes the source pixel P to the corresponding output, so for `src[0] = 0` the EPX rule writes 0 to `epx_buf[0]` and the check always failed. Fix: `t_9square_viewport` and `t_panel` now `memset(epx_buf, 0xCC, ...)` before calling and check `epx_buf[0] != 0xCC`. `t_epx_2x` keeps the `{10,20,10,20}` input but documents that all four EPX neighbour predicates miss on this pattern (so output is the P-fallback column-stripe), with new expectations `dst[0]==10 && dst[1]==10 / dst[2]==20 && dst[3]==20 / ...`. Probe mirrors the same sentinel approach. Local verification: `ctest -R csb_v2|csb_v22|dm1_v2_shape_runtime` 12/12, `firestaff_csb_v2_texture_upscale_probe` 13/13, `test_csb_v2_texture_upscale_pc34` 30/30.

- ✅ 2026-06-27 in-game high-contrast overlay gate (gap "High-contrast presentation hardening: launcher output is remapped to a restricted high-contrast palette; remaining work is in-game overlay coverage."). New `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` module (header + src) owns the M11-side gate state sourced from `M12_Config.highContrast`. The launcher pushes the same config bit into `M11_HighContrast_SetActive()` from `m12_apply_loaded_config()` (`src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c`) right after the existing `M11_UIScale_SetPercent` / `M11_Ambient_SetEnabled` push, so the in-game chrome uses the same restricted palette as the launcher when the toggle is on. The gate covers HUD text styles (`g_text_small`, `g_text_shadow`, `g_text_title`), dialog choice text, action-area / rune-strip text, combat-log text, hit-flash text, and the death / winner overlay text by routing `m11_draw_text` and `m11_draw_text_original` through a `m11_chrome_remap_style()` helper that builds a stack-local `M11_TextStyle` with `M11_HighContrast_RemapPresentedColor()` applied to both the foreground and shadow indices when the gate is on (default off → identity). The 320x200 dungeon-viewport pixel data and the HUD panel C040 / C017 backdrop blits are deliberately preserved bit-exact because raw viewport pixels are painted via separate bitmap-blit paths (`m11_draw_viewport`, the per-cell wall/floor/door/creature blits) and never go through `m11_draw_text`. `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBA()` exposes a region apply with a 16-bit `excludeMask` so callers can fence off the dungeon-viewport subrect even on chrome overlays; `M11_HighContrast_GetManifest()` returns a stable, parseable string documenting the coverage / preserve / default-state contract. New CTest `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` PASS 369/369 (default-off identity, toggle round-trip, restricted-palette remap when on with full 0..255 input sweep, manifest string contract, region apply gate off → no-op, region apply gate on with no exclude, region apply gate on with excludeMask, region clipping with negative origin / over-large rect / zero-area / NULL fb / zero dimensions, out-of-range index handling under excludeMask, launcher / game palette parity). New headless probe `firestaff_m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` PASS 14/14 (default-off state, launcher-config-driven gate push, chrome remap under gate, simulated 320x200 viewport fence preserving dungeon scene, HUD chrome strip remap outside the fence, toggle round-trip restores V1 identity, manifest documents gap closure). Registered as `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` + `m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` with labels `tier2;m11;accessibility;high-contrast`. Source-lock: none required — pure accessibility glue that mirrors the existing `m12_presented_color()` contract in `src/ui/menu_startup_m12.c` and adds the in-game counterpart; ReDMCSB does not cover high-contrast palette remap. **2026-06-28 rectangle-fence apply helper hardened the viewport fence:** new `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBAExceptRect()` exposes the explicit rectangle-fence variant of the region apply so a broad chrome-overlay pass can skip a precise dungeon-viewport rectangle (e.g. `0,0,224,136` over the 320x200 logical buffer) instead of relying only on palette-index `excludeMask` bit-fencing. The fence is evaluated BEFORE `excludeMask`, so a muted palette index inside the preserve rectangle is NEVER touched (the original dungeon scene stays bit-identical even when those pixels would otherwise collapse to BLACK); pixels outside the preserve rectangle still follow the restricted-palette remap. A non-positive `preserveWidth` / `preserveHeight` disables the rectangle fence and falls back to the existing `excludeMask`-only contract. The new helper is wired into a shared `m11_high_contrast_apply_active_region()` static implementation so the original `M11_HighContrast_ApplyActiveRGBA()` retains its `excludeMask`-only contract unchanged (callers that pass `0,0,0,0` for the preserve rectangle get identical behavior). Manifest string gets the new `chrome_rect_remap_with_viewport_fence` coverage token so downstream tools can audit the new helper by name. New CTest `m11_high_contrast_overlay_pc34_compat` PASS 379/379 (the original 369 + 10 new rectangle-fence assertions covering broad remap reports chrome changes, preserve rectangle stays byte-identical, chrome outside the rectangle follows the remap table, zero-area preserve rect disables the rectangle fence and falls back to excludeMask, negative preserve dimension disables the rectangle fence, gate off leaves every pixel alone even with a real preserve rect, manifest coverage entry). Headless probe `firestaff_m11_high_contrast_overlay_runtime_probe` PASS 19/19 (the original 14 + 5 new invariants covering rect-fenced broad remap touches HUD chrome strip, rect-fenced broad remap preserves dungeon viewport pixels, rect-fenced broad remap collapses chrome strip to BLACK, zero-area preserve rect disables the rectangle fence, rect-fence helper preserves checker pattern inside the dungeon viewport). The `m11_ui_scale`, `m11_phase_a`, and `m11_session_timer_runtime` CTest targets still PASS unchanged. `git diff --check` clean; `-Wall -Wextra -O2` clean on every new + touched file. Source-lock: none — still pure accessibility glue; the new helper is a strict superset of the existing `ApplyActiveRGBA()` and stays inside the same access boundary.

- ✅ 2026-07-01 launcher fallthrough views navigation-anchor gate (subtest N in `firestaff_m12_launcher_screen_reader_manifest_probe`). Pins the documented "out of scope" fallthrough contract for the 12 launcher views that intentionally fall through to `emit_main_view` as a navigation anchor: `M12_MENU_VIEW_DATA_VALIDATOR` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_AUDIO_SETTINGS` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_ACCESSIBILITY` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_THEME` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_SAVE_BROWSER` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_INPUT_REMAP` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_CUSTOM_DUNGEON` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_CAMPAIGN` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_SPELL_REFERENCE` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_MAP_VIEWER` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_TOUCH_LAYOUT` / `M12_MENU_VIEW_PRESENTATION_PREVIEW`. For each of the 12 views, the subtest asserts (a) the envelope `gameState` matches the active view (`launcher_<viewName>` — screen reader can announce "launcher theme" instead of "launcher main"), (b) the `GAME_CARD_DM1` / `MENU_SETTINGS` / `MENU_MUSEUM` / `GAME_CARD_THERON` navigation anchors are emitted, (c) the framebuffer dims stay pinned to 480x270, and (d) no foreign view markers leak into the manifest (the forbidden-marker table covers `ROW_*`, `TAB_*`, `CHANGELOG_LINE_*`, `MANUAL_DOC_*`, `BESTIARY_CAT_*`, `BESTIARY_ROW_*`, `ITEM_CAT_*`, `ITEM_ROW_*`, `SCREENSHOT_ROW_*`, `MUSEUM_CATEGORY_*`, `MUSEUM_BULLET_*`, `POPUP_MESSAGE`, `POPUP_OK`, `POPUP_LINE*`). The leak marker is printed in the probe log so a regression report tells the operator exactly which view-family leaked. The probe grew from 91/91 PASS to 175/175 PASS (84 new invariants, 7 per view × 12 views). The subtest is header-driven from a small `FallthroughViewSpec` table so adding the 13th view only takes one row. A future dedicated emitter for any of these 12 views only needs to assert that the new view-specific markers appear AND the fallthrough markers disappear — the navigation-anchor contract is already pinned. Source-lock: none required — pure accessibility/automation contract on top of public launcher state, same scope as the existing launcher manifest probe. ReDMCSB does not cover the launcher.

- ✅ 2026-06-19 pass841 (FTL swoosh 4bpp-packed buffer treated as 1-byte-per-pixel — user-reported v2.9.0 macOS arm64 regression): the FTL swoosh intro animation displayed as a half-blank vertically-striped image on Apple Silicon because `SWSH_Compat_ExpandLogoToBitmap` writes Atari ST low-res 4bpp-packed (32000 bytes, 2 pixels/byte) into a buffer the runtime treats as 1-byte-per-pixel indexed (64000 bytes). Pixels 160..319 of every row stayed zero (logo only rendered in the left half) and even pixels 0..159 showed alternating nibbles (vertical stripes). Fix: new helper `m11_swsh_unpack_4bpp_to_indexed` in `src/engine/main_loop_m11.c` (mirrors the existing `m11_unpack_title_4bpp_to_indexed` already used by the DM title path); dedicated 32000-byte packed buffer for SWSH expansion, then unpack into 64000-byte indexed buffer before palette/RGBA conversion. Also removed dead `paletteDirty` flag in `m11_play_ftl_swoosh_if_available` (was initialized to 0, never set to 1, so the WAIT_VBLANKS `if (paletteDirty) render` branch was unreachable). Source-lock against ReDMCSB Atari ST VDI / LINEA F0080_vq_extend / F0086_vs_clip low-res Physbase layout. Verification: `probes/v1/firestaff_v1_ftl_swoosh_palette_regression_probe.c` — 9/9 invariants incl. F841_SWSH_BUG_PACKED_DETECTED + F841_SWSH_UNPACK_VALID + F841_SWSH_UNPACK_COVERAGE + 4 load-bearing palette invariants; pre-fix sha256 `56549f3a...` post-fix `6612c1b1...`. ASCII companion `probes/v1/firestaff_v1_ftl_swoosh_ascii_probe.c` dumps the unpacked logo for eyeball regression check. CTest: `ftl_swoosh_palette_regression` + `ftl_swoosh_ascii_sanity` PASS, full suite 699/699 green (was 692/696 before parity-evidence watchdog churn unrelated to this fix).

- ✅ 2026-06-22 dosbox-debug / xvfb-run / unlzexe / wine shim stack on firestaff capture host: installed the four host shims that the pass235 entry-capture path now needs. `/opt/homebrew/bin/dosbox-debug` is a symlink to `/opt/homebrew/Cellar/dosbox-x/2026.06.02/bin/dosbox-x` (DOSBox-X 2026.06.02 ships an in-tree debugger with `BP` / `BPM` / `CPU` / `REG` / `DUMP` and `Alt+Pause` to enter, which is the modern replacement for the historical `dosbox-debug` binary). `/opt/homebrew/bin/xvfb-run` is a `/tmp/xrun` shim that starts Xvfb on a free `:90..:99` display, exports `DISPLAY`, runs the requested command under it, and tears the X server down on exit (macOS bash 3.2 treats `-X` flags as `exec` builtin options, so the shim routes everything through `bash -c 'exec "$0" "$@"' "$target" "$@"` instead of a plain `exec "$@"`). `/opt/homebrew/bin/unlzexe` is a symlink to the native `~/openclaw/data/unlzexe/unlzexe` LZEXE v0.91 unpacker (produces the expected sha256 `fc79ac65046e3d96c189ac3dd20ad40bacb8debee2cd1c7d2c33ca2d8f82fe94`, size 178224 — same as the historical `unlzexe.exe` output). `/opt/homebrew/bin/wine` is a thin dispatcher that maps `wine unlzexe.exe Z:<packed>` to the native unpacker, appends `.EXENEW` to the output filename when only one positional arg is given, and strips the historical `Z:` DOS-path prefix from any further args (the firestaff harnesses all use the `Z:` convention so the shim matches the original wine behaviour one-for-one). `tools/pass235_dm1_v1_dosbox_debugger_workflow.py` now spawns dosbox-debug via `pexpect.spawn` under a private Xvfb with `-nogui -o quit warning=false`, which is the correct combination for macOS ARM64 dosbox-x 2026.06.02: the in-tree debugger is unavailable against a pipe STDIN/STDOUT, and the Cocoa Quit-warning modal otherwise swallows SIGTERM. Observed on this host: dosbox-debug starts, FIRES.EXENEW is produced (sha256 matches), dosbox-x reaches `COMMAND.COM stack: 0x0749`, but the (Running)->-> break still does not surface against the pexpect-owned PTY (transcript_length 2840 bytes, no `01ED:0000` / `BADA26` / `CS=` hit) — the real Terminal.app launch path is required to land the F0128/F0380/F0267 runtime evidence row.

- ✅ 2026-06-23 DM1 V1 Hall of Champions portrait-20 cancel_reopen byte-stability hardening (gate 092): extended the existing `firestaff_dm1_v1_hall_of_champions_portrait_20_cancel_reopen_portrait_rect_position_runtime_probe` (added in the prior pass140 gate) with a new Group E section that asserts the D1C destination rectangle is byte-stable across the `pre-select -> post-cancel` half of the cancel_reopen cycle. The pre-select pose (panel off, championCount=0, ordinal=20) and the post-cancel pose (panel off after F0282 C162, championCount=0, ordinal=20) are observationally equivalent for the D1C cutout at `(96, 35, 32, 29)` — the C040 panel chrome is fully cleared by the C162 cancel branch and the C127 sensor on the front square is still sensorData=20 — so the same C026 portrait blit must hit the same 928 cells. The new Group E locks this with two byte-equality assertions: the D1C rect `(96, 35, 32, 29)` is byte-identical (0/928 cells differ) and the wider D1C row band `(96, 35, 32, 30)` including the 1px border below the portrait is also byte-identical (0/960 cells differ). This is a stronger invariant than the existing Group C match-based checks (which use a `>= 90%` aggregate C026 match threshold and tolerate a 10% mismatch). Any non-zero diff in the D1C area would be a regression in the cancel path — e.g. C040 chrome not fully cleared, panel backdrop leaking through the portrait cutout, or off-by-one border bug. The 19-cancel_reopen companion probe does not assert byte-stability; this is the non-duplicative hardening for ordinal 20. explicit selector-binding proof before it can promote a DGN render plan. The
existing material-raster test supplies that proof only as a controlled host
fixture; production remains blocked without a Saturn executable/capture route.
